page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.large is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The processor features 35 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, while baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements position the server in entry-tier performance brackets across CPU and memory tests. The instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 912.0 and a multi-core score of 1991.0, both placing in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems. PassMark results show a CPU score of 3617.68 and a memory score of 1241.98. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 20.95 GB/sec, while write operations reach 18.75 GB/sec. Data processing tasks reflect this profile, yielding 18.76 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 2.42 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to its standard resource density, trading high-frequency processing for fixed, non-burstable core allocation. The lack of integrated local storage necessitates attaching remote block storage for operating system and application data. Given these trade-offs, the ecs.sn1.large is suitable for predictable, low-demand tasks such as lightweight batch processing, entry-level continuous integration workers, internal utility services, and basic web routing layers that fit within an 8.0 GB memory envelope.
